Container.Name: ha-login-approval
Container.Overview:
Approve or reject sign-ins from a Home Assistant push notification. Truly PASSWORDLESS login, acting as a generic OIDC identity provider compatible with ZITADEL, Keycloak, Authentik, or any standard OIDC-capable relying party. Includes one-time recovery codes, IP blocking after 3 failed attempts, optional GeoIP enrichment, and a full admin panel.
Full step-by-step guide (registering the IDP in ZITADEL/Keycloak/Authentik, the admin panel, every variable): https://github.com/Nebur692/ha-login-approval
Admin panel: http://IP:8000/admin
Container.Requires: Home Assistant (with the Companion App installed on at least one device) and an OIDC-capable identity provider (ZITADEL, Keycloak, Authentik...) where you'll register this service as a generic external identity provider.

Config.Name: HA Base URL
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Your Home Assistant's internal URL, no trailing slash. Example: http://192.168.1.50:8123. This container calls Home Assistant's REST API and WebSocket to send push notifications and read the approve/reject action back.

Config.Name: HA Token
Config.Description: REQUIRED. A Home Assistant long-lived access token (Profile -> Security -> Long-Lived Access Tokens, at the bottom of the page). Needs permission to call notify.* services and to read mobile_app_notification_action events over the WebSocket.

Config.Name: Admin Username
Config.Description: Username for this container's own /admin panel. Plain HTTP Basic auth — this is a small internal tool, not a full user/session system.

Config.Name: Admin Password
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Password for the /admin panel, paired with Admin Username above.

Config.Name: Web/API Port
Config.Description: Internal port. Used for the /admin panel and as the base for the identity provider's own URLs (authorize/token/jwks, built from IDP Issuer URL below).

Config.Name: Persistent data
Config.Description: Persistent folder for this service's own SQLite database (the account directory, recovery codes, audit log, IP blocks, branding) and for the optional GeoIP .mmdb files. Without this volume, everything resets whenever the container is recreated — do not skip it.

Config.Name: IDP Issuer URL
Config.Description: REQUIRED. The PUBLIC https:// URL your identity provider (ZITADEL/Keycloak/Authentik) and the browser of whoever is signing in both use to reach this service. Must be a real domain behind a reverse proxy with a valid TLS certificate (nginx, Nginx Proxy Manager, Traefik, Caddy...) — NOT a local/LAN IP address, or nobody will be able to sign in from outside your own network. Example: https://login.yourdomain.com. Used as the OIDC issuer (iss claim) and to build the /authorize, /token, and /jwks.json URLs.

Config.Name: IDP Client ID
Config.Description: REQUIRED. The identifier your identity provider will present when authenticating against this service's /token endpoint. You make this value up yourself (e.g. ha-login-approval) — it must exactly match the Client ID you enter when registering this service as a generic external OIDC provider in your ZITADEL/Keycloak/Authentik.

Config.Name: IDP Client Secret
Config.Description: REQUIRED. A long, random secret you generate yourself, paired with IDP Client ID above — again, it must exactly match what you enter on the identity provider's side when registering this service.

Config.Name: IDP Client Redirect URI
Config.Description: REQUIRED. The exact callback URL your identity provider redirects to after a successful login (for ZITADEL, typically https://your-zitadel-domain/idps/callback). Validated on every request — a mismatch is rejected outright, to prevent an open redirect.

Config.Name: Approval Timeout Seconds
Config.Description: How many seconds to wait for an approve/reject tap on the phone before giving up and treating the login as failed.

Config.Name: Recovery/retry delay (seconds)
Config.Description: Seconds with no response before the bridge page offers to resend the notification or use a one-time recovery code instead. The original approval keeps waiting in the background too, so a late tap on the phone still works normally.

Config.Name: IP block threshold
Config.Description: Consecutive failures (an explicit Reject, or a wrong recovery code — same account plus same IP) before that account+IP pair is blocked. Not a time window, a straight consecutive-failure counter; any success resets it back to zero. Unblock manually from /admin/blocked-ips.

Config.Name: Recovery code batch size
Config.Description: How many one-time recovery codes get generated at once from the /admin/recovery panel. Generating a new batch instantly invalidates every code from the previous one.

Config.Name: Recovery code low warning
Config.Description: Push a warning notification once this many unused recovery codes (or fewer) remain for an account, so you notice before running out entirely.

Config.Name: MaxMind Account ID (GeoIP, optional)
Config.Description: OPTIONAL. A free MaxMind (maxmind.com) account ID, used to download the self-hosted GeoLite2-City/ASN databases and add city/country/ISP to both the audit log and the push notification itself. Left empty, that part of the audit log and notification just stays blank — login still works exactly the same.

Config.Name: MaxMind License Key (GeoIP, optional)
Config.Description: OPTIONAL, used together with the Account ID above. The license key generated in your MaxMind account settings.
